_comment: Cleared source data for the Hormuz tracker. Only licence-cleared inputs may appear in this file. See ../../company-memory/methodology.md.

source.table: Table 4. Volume of crude oil, condensate, petroleum products, and liquefied natural gas transported through the Strait of Hormuz
source.next_release_note: EIA does not publish a specific next-release date for the Global Energy Security Data supplement. Do not copy the parent STEO's next-release date here - they are different schedules. Derive staleness from release_date and the coverage end of the latest series row.
source.licence: U.S. federal government work, public domain; free to use and distribute with acknowledgement
source.attribution: Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Global Energy Security Data, released 12 August 2026. EIA volumes are based on Vortexa tanker tracking data with additional EIA analysis.
source.provenance_caveat: EIA analysis based on Vortexa tanker tracking data. We republish EIA's published analysis; we do not hold or license Vortexa data.
source.publisher_caveat: Since the end of February 2026, AIS signal data for ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz have become especially unreliable. For 2026 Hormuz volumes, tanker tracking data are being revised frequently based on the best available information.

model.regime_rule: Regime detector v2. calm if the latest quarter-on-quarter change in Hormuz total oil is within +/-10%. Otherwise disrupted, and sub-classified using companion chokepoints from the same cleared EIA table: 'local' if the control group (Danish Straits + Turkish Straits + Panama Canal, none of which carry Gulf barrels) moved less than 10% and diverged from Hormuz by more than 20 points - i.e. the strait moved and the rest of the world did not; 'systemic' if they moved together. See methodology.md section 5.
model.daily_estimate_authorised_by: Owner decision, 2026-09-17, on PR #4 (GitHub comment 5716791659): publish the model's daily estimate as the headline, with the word 'estimated' in the title. Supersedes the CEO's prior recommendation to headline the measured quarter. See critical issue #5 and decisions-log.md.
model.shape_function: GPCI transit-share: the strait is assumed to carry the same share of Gulf producer crude output (GPCI) as in the latest published quarter; the estimate moves monthly with GPCI. Replaced persistence on 2026-09-23 (methodology.md section 19).

estimate.band_basis: Re-derived each run from the estimator's own one-quarter-ahead back-test (model.estimator.backtest). Disrupted regime, Gulf production rising since 2Q26: from persistence (4.9, the anchor volume unchanged) to the estimator's worst measured miss, factor k=1.945, applied in the direction production moved.
estimate.label_required: Must be presented as an estimate, never as a measurement, and never without the band. Rubric section 1.6.

model.staleness_note: Regenerated daily by scripts/refresh_estimate.py (GitHub Actions). The job re-fetches both EIA sources, re-dates the estimate, recomputes point and band from the GPCI transit-share estimator and its own back-test, re-anchors on each new EIA quarter and scores the estimate it had published for that quarter against the measured figure (and against persistence). It fails loudly and publishes nothing if either fetch or parse fails, if GPCI does not cover the whole anchor quarter, or if the newest GPCI month is more than 70 days old. Past max_horizon_days beyond the anchor's coverage end the point estimate is suppressed entirely, because the method is only back-tested one quarter ahead.
model.companion_series_note: Companion chokepoint volumes from Table 2 of the same EIA Global Energy Security Data supplement (same publication, same public-domain licence as the Hormuz anchor). Used by the regime detector only; they do not enter the point estimate. Danish/Turkish/Panama carry no Gulf barrels and act as a global-demand control group.

estimator.name: GPCI transit-share estimator (option C, critical issue #9)
estimator.formula: estimate = (Hormuz total oil in anchor quarter / GPCI averaged over anchor quarter) x GPCI in latest history month
estimator.band_rule: calm: point +/- max(3%, 1.5 x worst calm back-test miss). disrupted: between persistence (anchor volume unchanged) and the estimator's worst measured disrupted miss (factor k) in the direction production has moved since the anchor quarter.

model.estimator_authorised_by: Owner closed critical issue #9 on 2026-09-23T10:34:58Z: 'Let's go with option C.' The CEO chose the construction (transit share of the latest published quarter x latest month of GPCI, i.e. option C as defined in the issue body, not the bypass-adjusted variant C-prime) under the methodology authority the owner granted in the same comment (GOVERNANCE.md). Published only on owner approval of the copy-review PR. See methodology.md section 19 and decisions-log.md 2026-09-23.

production_source.table: Table 3d. World Crude Oil Production (workbook STEO_m.xlsx, sheet 3dtab)
production_source.licence: U.S. federal government work, public domain; free to use and distribute with acknowledgement
production_source.construction: GPCI = crude oil production of Iran + Iraq + Kuwait + Saudi Arabia + Bahrain, history months only. UAE and Qatar excluded (carried only as total liquids, a different variable); Oman excluded (its export terminals are outside the strait). An index, not a measure of the strait.
